The melting process was proceeded in crucible resistance furnace and protected from oxidation by a flux cover.
Then the melt was heated to 780 ℃, and held at this temperature for 10 minutes.
After that, the melt was cooled to 750 ℃ and stewed for 15 minutes.
Then the melt was skimmed, and poured into a cast iron mould preheated to 300 ℃ to produce a columned ingot.

The lattice structures of magnesium and yttrium are all hexagonal-close-packed (hcp) structure, and their lattice constants are close to each other. Therefore, yttrium can be used as the nucleating agents to refine the microstructure of magnesium alloys.

As one of the surface-active elements, yttrium segregated at the solid-liquid interface during solidification. It turns out that Mg 2Si grew isotropically, and its growth velocity was decreased. As a result, the Mg 2Si was refined and its morphology was also modified.
dynamic recrystallization of α-Mg occurred, the α-Mg grains was refined (Fig. 4a)
thermally stable fine Mg 2Si particles located in the grain boundaries pinned the grain boundaries firmly and impeded the grain boundary gliding, thus the grain-boundary was strengthened effectively
the room temperature mechanical properties of the alloy were improved by both fine-grain strengthening and dispersion strengthening.
The improved elevated temperature properties of extruded Mg-1Y-1Si alloy are ascribed to the fine-grained strengthening and dispersion strengthening form Mg 2Si and ε-Mg 24 +x Y5 particles.
The higher elongation of the alloy at elevated temperature results from intracrystalline slip.
